\newcommand{\SIR}{\operatorname{S-I-R}}

# Set up details and utilities
Load required modules.
Note that `EpidemicsCFTP` is under development, while `FigureUtilities` needs in due course
to be pre-compiled!
```{julia}
using Colors, Compose, DataFrames, Measures
import Cairo, Fontconfig, Gadfly
gf = Gadfly

using EpidemicsCFTP 
```

Use `make clean` if it becomes necessary to force re-compilation of all cells,
including this one in particular. (Though this still seems flakey! best way
seems to be to force a new computation in the relevant cell.)
```{julia}
include("./FigureUtilities.jl")
using .FigureUtilities ;
```

Here are some very basic features about the epidemic.
```{julia}
const population = 6 ;
const duration   = 3 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```


## Style choices
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch);
```

For now, use default style from `FigureUtilities`.
```{julia}
style = defaultstyle ;
```

## Dealing with different kinds of incident
It is convenient to abbreviate various types of incident.
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection
R = Removal            ; C = CRemoval   
I = Infection          ; P = PInfection
IR = InitialRemoved    ; II = InitialInfected    ; IS = InitialSusceptible
CR = ContinuingRemoved ; CI = ContinuingInfected ; CS = ContinuingSusceptible
MIA = MarkerInfectionA ; MRA = MarkerRemovalA
MIB = MarkerInfectionB ; MRB = MarkerRemovalB ;
```

# Experiments
Plot regions of infection and removal. First define an epidemic
and compute its total trajectory.
```{julia}
env0 = Innovation(5, 
  A[I(0.11,2,3), I(0.2,2,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), 
    I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), P(1.1,2,3), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), 
    I(1.5,3,4)], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2), R(1.55,1),
    R(1.85,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)] ) ;
```


```{julia}
initial= SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
chron  = chronology(env0) ; states = [initial] # both will be overwritten
traj, realized = evolution_recurse!(states, AbstractIncident[], duration, chron, conditioned=true)

infect1   = [x for x in realized if isa(x, I) || isa(x, P)]
infect2   = [(MIA(x.t, x.infectee-1), MIB(x.t, x.infectee)) for x in infect1]
remove1   = [x for x in realized if isa(x, C) || isa(x, R)]
remove2   = [(MRA(x.t, k-1), MRB(x.t, k)) for (k, x) in enumerate(remove1)]
realized2 = sort(vcat(infect2, remove2), lt=(x,y) -> isearlier(x[1], y[1]))
realized_trajectory = collect(Iterators.flatten(realized2));
total_trajectory = compute_total_trajectory(duration, population, initial, realized);
```

## Plot regions of infection and removal
```{julia}
regions = region_plot(duration, population, total_trajectory)

depict("Regions", compose(context(units=coordinates), regions))
```
Add removals and conditional removals.
```{julia}
removal_incidents = (context(),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in env0.removals  if isa(inc, R)]),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in env0.cremovals if isa(inc, C)]),
  )
depict("Removals", compose(context(units=coordinates), (removal_incidents, regions)...))
```

## Consider now the construction of "no-infection" zones.

First: construct the separate timelines.
```{julia}
removal_list_of_lists = [Float64[] for k in (1:population)]
cremoval_list = C[]
for incident in chronology(env0)
  if isa(incident, R)
    push!(removal_list_of_lists[incident.target], incident.t)
  elseif isa(incident, C)
    push!(cremoval_list, incident)
  end
end

println(cremoval_list)
removal_structure = collect(enumerate(removal_list_of_lists))
```

Now isolate the time-lines containing a `MIB`, and insert a `0.0` at start.
```{julia}
proto_no_infections_zones = [Float64[] for k in (1:population)]
for marker in total_trajectory
  if isa(marker, MIB)
    timeline = removal_structure[marker.target][2]
    banned_removals = [x for x in timeline if x < marker.t]
    if length(banned_removals) > 0
      proto_no_infections_zones[marker.target] = [0.0, maximum(banned_removals)]
    end
  end
end

pniz = enumerate(proto_no_infections_zones)

zone1 = (context(), 
          line([[(pp, xl[1]) for pp in xl[2]] for xl in pniz if length(xl[2])>0]),
          defaultstyle.broad, stroke(defaultstyle.forbid), fillopacity(0.25),
        )

depict("TestNoInfection", compose(context(units=coordinates),
                                 (removal_incidents, 
                                  FigureUtilities.draw_realized_elements(initial, realized),
                                  FigureUtilities.draw_elements(env0),
                                  regions, zone1)...)
      )
```

Now also add in the potential infections.

# Computing the last viable epidemic
First establish realized removal incidents in time-decreasing order
of _removed_ timeline
(easily done: the \(i^\text{th}\) realized removal listed in time-order
will necessarily remove time-line \(i\)),
and list potential infections prior to each realized removal
according to infection time.
Notice we have not yet covered the possibility that some time-lines
are never infected and others are not removed before `duration`
(the end of the simulation). Notice too that the first time-line
is (of course) infected at time \(0\) and is not otherwise infected.

```{julia}
realized_removals = filter(x -> (isa(x, R) || isa(x, C)), realized)
reversed_removals = reverse(collect(enumerate(realized_removals))[2:end])
barrier = reversed_removals[1][2]
last_viable = []
for (k, rem) in reversed_removals
  println("Timeline $k ends at $rem, at time $(rem.t)")
  prior_removals = [pr for pr in env0.removals if pr.target==k && pr.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior rem) ", join([string(pr) for pr in prior_removals], " "))
  prior_infections = [pf for pf in env0.infections if pf.infectee==k && pf.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior inf) ", join([string(pf) for pf in prior_infections], " "))
  barrier =
      sort( [pf for pf in prior_infections if pf.t < barrier.t], by=x -> x.t)[end]
  println("  (last viable infection) ", barrier)
  println("\n")
  pushfirst!(last_viable, barrier)
end
println("  (last_viable) ", join([string(pr) for pr in last_viable], " "))
```

By the nature of the simulation, no prior potential infections will infect
a time-line _after_ it has been removed, because by then the `target` time-line
must also have been removed.
